look_here_first: Look at the climbing organ first: trumpet creeper clings with short aerial rootlets, then confirm the large opposite odd-pinnate leaves with 7–11 sharply serrated leaflets.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: climbs by short aerial rootlets rather than tendrils

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: commonly 7–11 ovate to lanceolate sharply serrated leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large orange to reddish-orange tubular/funnelform flowers in terminal clusters

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: four fertile didynamous stamens plus a staminode

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: long narrow 2-valved capsule with many flattened winged seeds

lookalikes.differences: The climbing organ is the fastest split from crossvine: rootlets in Campsis versus branched adhesive tendrils in Bignonia.
